correctness.rationale: Final assessment of repairs/2/RESULT.md. The frozen edge narrative is not literally correct for r>1/[2(1−s)]: A(rv3) lies past R(rv0), in the next corner segment (e.g. at r=0.9 their horizontal coordinates are about 0.582 and 0.418). The corrected proof joins the last corner image and the bottom image into the entire collinear arc [rv3,R(rv1)]; their intermediate image join is allowed to move. The corner radial charts and bottom slices exhaust the annulus and leave the finding unchanged. Independently, each corner-strip Jacobian is rtδ from det B=1; the bottom Jacobian is t(1−r), deriving M without a finite shoelace check. Area invariance gives leafwise invariance a.e.; weak continuity of the strip measures extends it to every leaf, including the degenerate bottom segment at r=1 where the period claim matters. Cumulative mass conjugates each leaf to translation by rtδ/M(r); the derivative is positive and the endpoint is 1/12. Substituting its inverse gives the stated cubic density and finite area. Fourier modes n≠0 have absolutely continuous spectral measures; n=12 with constant radial factor gives a measure equivalent to Haar. Mode zero and the Riemann–Lebesgue lemma give exactly the stated eigenspace and decay on its orthogonal complement. I reviewed the frozen verification and checker without executing the uploaded script. The final corrected analytic steps, not the finite script, establish the claims.

originality.rationale: For the repaired scope the supported distinct results are the full outer-annulus radial rotation function and continuous area-density law, and the resulting map-specific spectral type. Neither invariant foliation, rational endpoint range, total annulus area, nor discrete slow-frequency sublevels are credited as new. The nearest results were compared by statement. The original article and thesis describe linear variation in the break-line segment coordinate; literally that is not the same as the actual fractional-linear law: on E1P1 the physical point is rP1 and the second derivative of the repaired rotation law is strictly positive. The strip proof independently determines the actual full-map rotation number rather than using endpoint interpolation.
residual_risks: Unidentified equivalent computations or unpublished derivations are possible; this is not a priority finding.
Only the outer annulus is audited. The larger foliation in the literature cannot be used to extend this spectral verdict to the square.
